title: Hickson Compact Group 87
caption: Hickson Compact Group 87, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Gemini South image shows Hickson Compact Group 87 (HCG 87), a group of galaxies in the direction of Capricornus. It was taken while the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) was being commissioned in early 2003, when both images and spectra of the group were obtained.

The result compares very favourably with a space-based image of the same field, showing how sharp Gemini's view can be when atmospheric conditions are at their best. Telescopes on the ground normally look through a turbulent atmosphere that blurs fine detail, so steady air makes a big difference.

A compact group is a small collection of galaxies packed closely together, near enough that their gravity can distort one another's shapes over time. Commissioning is the testing period when a new instrument is checked and tuned before regular science observations begin, and a clear view like this one helps demonstrate what it can do.

understand.summary: Taken with GMOS on Gemini South; the filters used and the colour mapping aren't published.
understand.eye: The telescope's large mirror and long exposure gather far more light than the eye, revealing faint detail in the galaxies.

explore: Gemini South stands on Cerro Pachón in Chile. This image covers about 4 by 4 arcminutes of sky, with each pixel spanning 0.073 arcseconds, and the observations were made on May 25, 2003.
